zh: Thomas Edward Lawrence (1888-1935) an English soldier and writer. He began his career as an archaeologist (= a person who studies ancient history by examining objects found under the ground), but in 1916 went to Saudi Arabia to plan and lead a successful military campaign against Turkish rule in the Middle East, as a result of which he became known as Lawrence of Arabia. He described the campaign in his book Seven Pillars of Wisdom (1926). This brought him fame and a romantic reputation, but he disliked publicity and tried to escape it by twice changing his name. He died in a motorcycle accident in Dorset, England. A film, Lawrence of Arabia, about his life appeared in 1962.
en: Thomas Edward Lawrence (1888-1935) an English soldier and writer. He began his career as an archaeologist (= a person who studies ancient history by examining objects found under the ground), but in 1916 went to Saudi Arabia to plan and lead a successful military campaign against Turkish rule in the Middle East, as a result of which he became known as Lawrence of Arabia. He described the campaign in his book Seven Pillars of Wisdom (1926). This brought him fame and a romantic reputation, but he disliked publicity and tried to escape it by twice changing his name. He died in a motorcycle accident in Dorset, England. A film, Lawrence of Arabia, about his life appeared in 1962.

zh: Thomas Stearns Eliot (1888-1965) a British poet, writer of plays, and literary critic (= person who gives opinions about works of literature), born in the US. Ezra Pound encouraged him to live in England, where from 1914 he made his home. Eliot's poems have had a great influence on other poets, particularly The Waste Land and Four Quartets. One of his most important new ideas was to use the natural rhythms of speech in his poetry. His best-known plays are Murder in the Cathedral (1935) and The Cocktail Party (1951). In 1948 he was given the Nobel Prize for literature.

en: to look or behave like an older member of your family, especially your mother or father
ex: Your daughter doesn't take after you at all.
你女儿长得一点儿都不像你。

en: to start not liking somebody/something for no clear reason

zh: （运动或比赛）轻易打败，把…打得一败涂地
en: to defeat somebody easily in a game or competition
ex: We were simply taken apart by the other team.
我们只是被另一支球队拆散了。

zh: （从餐馆买饭菜等）带回食用；买外卖食物
en: to make a feeling, pain, etc. disappear
ex: I was given some pills to take away the pain.
给我开了一些止痛药片。

en: to make the effort or value of something seem less
ex: I don't want to take away from his achievements, but he couldn't have done it without my help.
我不想贬低他的成就，但是如果没有我的帮助，他是做不成的。

zh: 允许（因不合而离去的配偶等）回家；与…重归于好
en: to allow somebody, such as your husband, wife or partner, to come home after they have left because of a problem
ex: The smell of the sea took him back to his childhood.
大海的气味使他回想起孩提时代。

en: to remove a structure, especially by separating it into pieces
ex: to take down a tent
拆掉帐篷

zh: to take somebody to a police station in order to ask them questions
en: to allow somebody to stay in your home
ex: to take in lodgers
收房客

en: to behave in an unpleasant way towards somebody because you feel angry, disappointed, etc., although it is not their fault
ex: OK, so you had a bad day. Don't take it out on me.
好，这么说你今天遇上了很多倒霉事。可也别拿我当出气筒。

zh: 突然大受欢迎；迅速流行
（以诙谐的方式）模仿，学某人的样子
en: to leave the ground and begin to fly
ex: The plane took off an hour late.
飞机起飞晚了一个小时。

zh: （运动或比赛）同某人较量；反抗；与某人战斗
决定做；同意负责；承担（责任）
en: to employ somebody
ex: to take on new staff
雇用新员工

zh: 带某人出去（到餐馆、剧院、俱乐部等）
切除，摘除（人体内的一部分）
获得，领到（正式文件或服务）
en: to go to a restaurant, theatre, club, etc. with somebody you have invited
ex: They took out two enemy bombers.
他们摧毁了敌人的两架轰炸机。

en: to remove an amount of money from a larger amount, especially as a payment
ex: The fine will be taken out of your wages.
罚款将从你的工资中扣除。

zh: 使摆脱苦恼；为某人消愁
en: to make somebody forget their worries and become less concerned with their own thoughts and situation

zh: 接收，接管（企业、公司等，尤指通过购买股份）
en: to become bigger or more important than something else; to replace something
ex: Try not to let negative thoughts take over.
尽量别受消极的想法左右。

en: Fifth Amendment

zh: 帮助某人深入了解；给某人解说
en: to help somebody learn or become familiar with something, for example by talking about each part in turn
ex: The director took us through the play scene by scene.
导演一幕一幕地给我们说戏。

en: to go away to a place, especially to escape from danger
ex: The rebels took to the hills.
反叛者躲进山里。

en: to continue, especially starting after somebody/something else has finished
ex: The band's new album takes up where their last one left off.
这个乐队的新唱片集是接上一集的乐曲录制的。

en: to question somebody about something, because you do not agree with them
ex: I must take you up on that point.
那个问题我一定要找你问个明白。

zh: 开始结交（尤指名声不好的人）
en: to begin to be friendly with somebody, especially somebody with a bad reputation
ex: They decided to take the matter up with their MP.
他们决定向本地区的下院议员反映这一问题。

zh: （扣除税项等之后的）实得工资
en: the amount of money that you earn after you have paid tax, etc.
the moment at which an aircraft leaves the ground and starts to fly
ex: The plane is ready for take-off.
飞机准备随时起飞。
